title: Choose the visual world
question: Safer hand: the roll is suspended. Pick from the remaining familiar grounded worlds, or play it straight against Foreplay, Motion, and the native Ad Library.

options.label: Swipe-File Binder
options.lineage: tabbed competitor swipe files, pulled pages, and grease-pencil selects on a strategist’s desk
options.thesis: Each ad is a pulled page in a working swipe file, not a dashboard card.
options.viewport: Binder tabs as URL lots; the table as pulled pages; a page lifted into a right-hand inspect.
options.risk: Swipe-file nostalgia can costume a table if the tabs are decoration.

options.label: Watch Desk
options.lineage: collection desks, source logs, and take folders from OSINT and media-monitoring rooms
options.thesis: The run is a collection job: sources first, take as it lands, judgment after.
options.viewport: Source URLs and job status on top; take table fills immediately; inspect is a pulled folder.
options.risk: Watch-desk chrome can feel ops-heavy if it hides the ad body.

options.label: As-Run Rundown
options.lineage: broadcast traffic rundowns: timed spots, as-run logs, and show clocks
options.thesis: URL i/5 is a rundown clock; each ad is a spot that has already run.
options.viewport: A rundown header with the clock; spots as dense rows; the selected spot opens the script.
options.risk: Broadcast dark-slate can bury copy if the clock outranks the log.

canonCard.label: Play it straight
canonCard.thesis: The category standard, aimed at Foreplay, Motion, and Meta’s own Ad Library: left query, center table, right drawer, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, URL input, filter row, results table, slide-over detail — what those products already trained the user to expect.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Foreplay / Motion by design.
